calibration.negativeControlsScopeNote: Three, at every-measured-target scope. "color remains fixed" is deliberately absent: it is what this control MOVES. The three that remain — type, stroke, motion — are orthogonal to a colour seed and held in every scenario measured, on both arms.
calibration.stopSemantics: A STOP IS A (ROLE, HEX) PAIR: the mutation of ONE role, not of the palette. Measured: each of primaryColor / secondaryColor / accentColor moves exactly its own ten ramp steps and crosses ZERO into another role, which is what makes the per-role negative decidable with an exact zero instead of a tolerance. The alternatives were refuted by absence, not by preference: no preset palette catalog exists anywhere in src (and that shape already has its own domain kind, profile-id, with its calibration.catalog law), and no hue-rotation mechanism exists (the ramp holds hue constant by design). An IDENTITY stop declares no value and resolves against the arm's own baseline: it is the first identity in this programme that differs per vertical (#FFFFFF / #3A6FB0 / #171717), and it fails closed rather than inventing one.

measuredResult.instrument: packages/core/src/tooling/resolution-probe, Chromium, --bundle fresh, Node 22.17.0, plus direct compiles through the productive doors for step 0 and the identity law.
measuredResult.step0Apca: RUN FIRST, BEFORE ANY STOP WAS AUTHORED, and it disqualified an axis. Every background candidate THROWS TenantThemeValidationError on the DB arm in 3/3 verticals: #123456 and #0B0B0C leave --ds-color-text-primary at APCA Lc 0.0 against the new ground, #F7F7F5 leaves --ds-color-text-muted/-disabled below the floor (Lc 48.2 / 50.2 / 36.2). The ground is NOT independently writable: it needs a paired foreground, which is a different stop shape. The background role is therefore NOT declared as a stop. The three role seeds compile in 3/3.
measuredResult.perRoleIsolation: Measured on deriveTenantColorRamps over a fixed 7-seed palette: primaryColor, secondaryColor and accentColor each move exactly 10 channels — their own role's ten steps — and 0 channels of any other role. backgroundColor moves 63 of 70: nine of ten steps in ALL SEVEN roles, including success/warning/error/info, which this control does not seed. The ground is the ramp ground, not a fourth peer seed. Drilled (F4B-8 drills 5 and 6).
measuredResult.identityLaw: W-A, measured on both arms. STATIC: writing the vertical's own value at the role keypath moves ZERO channels — 3 roles x 3 verticals, nine cases, all zero. The identity law holds exactly. DB: it does NOT — writing the vertical's own colour still emits a non-empty delta (bithire 7 vars, evnto 5, the same count for all three roles, so it is colour-independent), and rottay/primary (#FFFFFF) even throws on APCA. The DB arm takes no baseline by law (H-1 V5), so an identity stop is a STATIC-ARM claim; the harness refuses it on the DB arm rather than inventing the vertical value there.
measuredResult.invalidSeedIsSilent: THE FALSE GREEN THIS CONTROL BRINGS, measured not theorised. A non-hex seed does not throw and does not produce NaN: hexToRgbFloat runs parseInt(value, 16), NaN >> 16 & 255 is 0 in JS, so the seed becomes BLACK and derives a plausible GREY ramp. rebeccapurple and rgb(59, 130, 246) — both valid CSS colours — collapse this way. The channel MOVES, so a probe asking "did it move?" certifies as live a control that discarded the tenant colour. The signature that betrays it: --ds-color-primary passes the raw string through, the ramp goes achromatic, and --ds-chart-series-1 DISAPPEARS (it is behind isHexColor; the ramp derivation is not). The color-set branch refuses non-hex for exactly this reason (drill 3).
measuredResult.scenariosRun: Six causal runs over two stops (primary/crimson #DC2626, primary/indigo #4F46E5) x three verticals, light and dark, full roster. rottay: REFUSED by the empty-lowering guard — the DB arm emits none of the declared channels. bithire: harness-live, restore exact on both arms, negatives held, and 10 divergent rows. evnto: same, 4 divergent rows. Both stops give identical divergence counts, so the divergence is a property of the axis, not of the colour.
measuredResult.witnessMatrix: Of the five declared channels, only --ds-color-primary and --ds-chart-series-1 move on all three verticals; --ds-color-primary-500 is inert on rottay (it authors all seven palette.ramps, which win over derivation); --ds-button-primary-bg and --ds-color-text-on-primary are inert on all three. --ds-color-primary is the only reliable direct witness, and structurally so: brand-theme:825 assigns it straight from the seed.

knownDefects.finding: MEASURED IN THE ARTIFACTS, not inferred. Each vertical artifact declares --ds-color-primary TWICE: at :is(html[data-tenant=X], :where([data-ds-root][data-vertical=X])) and again at that SAME selector plus [data-theme='dark'] (rottay: .light). bithire index.css:323 and :1371 are the two lines. The mode block carries one extra attribute, so it outranks the static arm's appended tenant block by SPECIFICITY — appending later does not help. The DB arm writes inline on the document element and is not outranked. Result: the static arm is structurally inert, in that mode, for every channel the artifact re-declares per mode. Accounts for all 7 dark rows on bithire and all 4 on evnto.
knownDefects.classNote: SUPERSEDED BY M-1, and the previous reading was WRONG rather than incomplete. It called this an instance of OPEN_VERTICAL_CASCADE_DEFECT owned by the vertical-artifact generator. M-1 measured the compilers and refuted that: the double declaration is the CORRECT OUTPUT of compileModeBlocks (a base block plus one block per authored non-default mode, under a one-attribute-stronger selector), and the two compilers AGREE in that mode — the tenant seed does not reach the overlay (bithire: base moves 22 channels, the dark block 0), and compileTenantThemeConfig even ADDS a dark delta re-asserting the vertical values (0 -> 29 vars) precisely to hold that line. The generator has no defect here. What was wrong was the INSTRUMENT: the static arm wrote only the base scope (fixed in M-1: it now emits 1+n blocks at the compiler's own themeModeSelector), and the DB arm still drops compiled modeDeltas and writes inline on the document element, where it outranks every mode block and produces a reading no production path produces. The remaining question — SHOULD a tenant seed move the non-default mode — is a PRODUCT adjudication, not a defect of this control.

The alias tracks the seed; the baked hex does not. Accounts for the three bithire LIGHT rows (the channel itself plus the button background-color and border-top-color it paints). evnto has no light divergence because both arms emit the alias there.

knownDefects.finding: The DB arm emits ZERO variables for every palette-seed write on rottay that compiles (#DC2626, #4F46E5, #3A6FB0 -> 0 vars; #22C55E and #A0A0A5 throw on APCA), while the same door emits a delta for density and typography on the same vertical. The harness refuses the run rather than reporting it, which is correct: an arm that emits none of the declared channels is a finding, not an arm.
knownDefects.designStageCorrection: This REFUTES the F4B-8 design prediction that rottay would be a DESIGNED_NULL with both arms equally inert. Measured, the arms diverge there rather than agreeing at zero. Recorded as a correction because the design said it in writing.

knownDefects.finding: The color-set branch refuses any non-hex stop value. That is a restriction OF THE HARNESS, not of the product: the DB compiler accepts functional colour syntax (tenant-theme-compiler.test.ts:1187). What the branch refuses to do is lower a value whose downstream meaning it cannot predict on both arms — measured, a non-hex seed goes silently grey through the ramp derivation while the isHexColor-guarded channels skip entirely.
